hooks.text: A massive star is spinning so fast it flings off its surface.
The center of Cassiopeia is a star slowly tearing itself to shreds.
Spinning at 450 kilometers per second, one star is tearing itself apart.

title: The Star Tearing Itself Apart in Cassiopeia
description: Gamma Cassiopeiae spins so violently it flings off its own gas, feeding a hidden white dwarf while vaporizing nearby ghost nebulae.

beats.text: A massive star is spinning so fast it flings off its surface.
beats.visual: Artist's illustration of rapidly rotating Be star with circumstellar decretion disk

beats.text: Located 550 light-years away, Gamma Cassiopeiae marks the central point of the celestial W in Cassiopeia.
beats.visual: Photograph of constellation Cassiopeia showing central star Gamma Cassiopeiae, 2020

beats.text: Rotating at roughly 450 kilometers per second, this bulged star is on the brink of structural breakup.
beats.visual: Computer simulation of rapidly rotating star distorted into an oblate spheroid

beats.text: Radiating 19,000 times more energy than the Sun, its intense radiation is actively vaporizing nearby nebulae.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope image of nebula IC 63, the Ghost of Cassiopeia, 2018

beats.text: For five decades, astronomers faced an unsolved puzzle: the star blazed with X-rays reaching 150 million degrees.
beats.visual: X-ray image of superheated plasma in high-energy binary system, Chandra, 2015

beats.text: In 2026, the XRISM space telescope unmasked the culprit by tracking Doppler shifts in the hot plasma.
beats.visual: Artist's impression of JAXA and NASA XRISM satellite in Earth orbit, 2023

beats.text: The radiation doesn't come from the giant, but from a hidden, Earth-sized white dwarf companion.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of white dwarf accreting gas from companion star, 2021

beats.text: Every 203 days, this dense corpse feeds on material shed by an unraveling giant.
beats.visual: Widefield astrophotograph of Gamma Cassiopeiae illuminating surrounding ghost nebulae, 2022

better_than_last: Replaced technical spectral terminology with clear physical speed and predator stakes, holding the 2026 XRISM breakthrough until beat 6 to sustain high midpoint retention before a clean loop.
